annotations.shape: one text/plain us-ascii-body message with 8-bit bytes in a header VALUE (`X-8bit: caf\xe9 \x81 end`); the value is viewed losslessly as latin-1 (D2), so the bytes 0xE9 and 0x81 are U+00E9 and U+0081 in the label
annotations.raw_fixture: hand-written bytes in tools/write_raw_fixtures.py, frozen in fixtures/raw/SHA256SUMS -- a generator writing UTF-8 text cannot emit the lone 8-bit byte 0x81
annotations.phase_0_facts: container.*, headers.fields (ordinal 3 keeps the raw 8-bit value as latin-1 text), part.tree, part.regions, part.gaps, body.preamble_epilogue, decode.chain and body.content_sha256; the BODY is plain ASCII, so the declared us-ascii charset decodes strictly
annotations.phase_1_facts: headers.projection (the raw value beside its parsed latin-1 view) and document.axes
annotations.labels_are_typed: every value was read out of the fixture bytes with a hex-editor-style line dump and typed by a model from the RFC and design rules (D2, D13), never copied out of the walker; labels_provenance is spec because a model wrote them, not a person
annotations.span_conventions: a field's raw_span covers its line including the line ending; value_span starts immediately after the colon and keeps the leading space; a byte span is counted in bytes, not characters, so the single-byte 0xE9 and 0x81 each count one
annotations.expected_gaps: none: 8-bit bytes in a header value are recorded verbatim and are not a malformed line (the name is ASCII)
annotations.not_yet_labelled: addresses, the Date projection, encoded words, body views, attachments, statuses, thread edges and TimeEvents
